answer: Hardware-bound identity relies on bus timing. Each node pins 64 GB of pseudorandom graphs to local DRAM. The verifier streams a challenge across the memory-bus jetty, commanding a non-sequential chase across the address knoll. The prover must traverse the chain and return a pearl hash within an 85-nanosecond budget per hop. Emulated or shared hardware routed over external links incurs millisecond latency spikes, instantly failing the timing proof and slashing the identity's 4000-token bond.
